A.  Brain, biopsy:  High-grade glioma with necrosis, consistent with glioblastoma; see comment.
B.  Brain, biopsy:  Malignant glioma consistent with glioblastoma; see comment.

Anatomic Site:Brain, biopsy (fs)
Right parietal tumor
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 55-year-old man with a rapidly growing brain mass, suspicious for glioblastoma.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received in three parts, each labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.
Part A is additionally labeled "tumor." It consists of multiple irregular fragments of neural tissue, with an aggregate measurement of 1.3 x 0.8 x 0.3 cm. Representative sections are submitted for frozen section diagnosis as FS1 and cytologic preparation, with the frozen section remnant submitted in cassette A1. The remainder is submitted in cassette A2.
Part B, additionally labeled "right parietal tumor--permanent," consists of a 2.5 x 1.5 x 0.4 cm, rectangular, firm tissue fragment. The specimen is entirely submitted in cassette B1.
Part C, labeled "right parietal tissue," consists of a 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.2 cm piece of white-gray, soft tissue, submitted entirely in cassette C1.
Diagnosis Comments:
This malignant neoplasm is composed of densely packed cells with pleomorphic nuclei and a high mitotic rate. Microvascular proliferation and areas of necrosis are evident. Although the morphological features are compatible with glioblastoma, differential diagnoses include metastatic carcinoma.
Immunohistochemical stains were performed and evaluated to establish the diagnosis and include GFAP, neurofilament, and p53 on A2, as well as keratin and vimentin on B1.
GFAP shows strong positive staining, while neurofilament shows infiltration of neoplastic cells. P53 shows strong positive staining, supporting the diagnosis of glioblastoma.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1  (A) Brain, biopsy:  Glioblastoma, WHO grade IV. Tissue section and cytologic preparation.  (Dr. Michael Nguyen, 69432.)
Final Diagnosis:
A.  Brain, right parietal, biopsy:  Glioblastoma (Astrocytoma WHO grade IV); see comment.
B.  Brain, right parietal, biopsy:  Glioblastoma (Astrocytoma WHO grade IV); see comment.
C.  Right parietal tissue, biopsy:  Glioblastoma, WHO grade IV; see comment.

Diagnosis Comments:

A.  Brain, biopsy:  Recurrent glioblastoma multiforme; see comment.
